name: Mandahuaca
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Ramirez, Henri 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: Comparação e Descrição (contains Mandahuaca material; etnolinguistica.org copy blocked by TLS cert mismatch)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page mand1448 and reference record 581555 (Ramirez 2020).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No descriptive references (Glottolog's most extensive description wordlist or less); subclassification reference Ramirez 2020 vol. II ch. 14, pp. 87-206; ELCat status dormant (extinct in Brazil in the 1990s, probably in Venezuela).

sources.citation: Aikhenvald, Alexandra Y. 1999. The Arawak language family. In Dixon & Aikhenvald (eds.), The Amazonian Languages, 65-106. Cambridge: CUP.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mandawaka (Mawaca) appears only as an extinct language in the table (p. 70) and in n. 3 p. 387 (source Koch-Grünberg 1911); the stress paragraph covers other Arawak languages, not Mandawaka.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1911. Aruak-Sprachen Nordwestbrasiliens und der angrenzenden Gebiete. Mitteilungen der Anthropologischen Gesellschaft in Wien 41: 33-153, 203-282.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: Aikhenvald 1999 cites it for Mandawaka (Mawaca); Koch-Grünberg 1928 says its Mandauáka list was 'fast ganz neu', so 1911 has at most a few Mandawaka words, but its comparative introduction may contain a general remark on accent in the Rio Negro Arawak languages.

sources.citation: Ferreira 2017 (Unicamp thesis on Arawak phonological systems).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mandawaka appears only in classification tables (marked extinct); no data.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005-. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: ARAWAK. Entry MANDAWAKA, pp. 81-83.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic guide only (location, speaker counts, bibliography: Aikhenvald 1995, Civrieux & Lichy 1950, Koch-Grünberg 1906/1911/1913, Nimuendajú 1932, Tavera-Acosta 1907, González Ñáñez 2000, Pérez 1988); nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: Comparação e Descrição. Manaus: EDUA. Sec. 4.2 'Os Mandawaka', pp. 337-339 (pdf 347-349); sec. 5.2, p. 468 (pdf 479).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number PM5476 .R36 2001
sources.note: Sec. 4.2 has no phonology: history, lexicostatistics from Koch-Grünberg's 312-word list, three grammatical morphemes, and a Mandawaka/Warekena comparative vocabulary reproducing Koch-Grünberg's accent marks (nu-né:ne 'tongue', nu-nú:ma 'mouth'). P. 468 states explicitly that for lack of data and adequate descriptions of Warekena, Mandawaka, Kauixana etc. the accent system of the Japurá-Colômbia group will not be discussed.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1932. Wortlisten aus Amazonien. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 24(1): 93-119. doi 10.3406/jsa.1932.1846.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Contains Mura, Mundurukú, Arikém and Parirí lists only; no Mandawaka material despite Fabre listing it under Mandawaka. Irrelevant.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1928. Vom Roroima zum Orinoco, Bd. IV: Sprachen. Stuttgart: Strecker und Schröder. 'Piapóko, Adzáneni, Mandauáka', pp. 287-301 (pdf 301-315).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The Mandauáka 'Charakter der Sprache' (p. 288) is a single line on the quality of l ('l nicht so rein wie im Adzáneni, aber nicht so unrein, wie in den Karibensprachen'); the wordlist carries acute accent marks on individual words but no rule of stress placement is stated.

sources.citation: Tavera-Acosta, Bartolomé. 1907. En el Sur (Dialectos indígenas de Venezuela). Ciudad Bolívar: Benito Jimeno Castro. Mandauaca vocabulary, Segunda Parte, three-column table Mandauaca/Yabitero/Uareca from p. 63; author's note (8) p. 63.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Note (8) on the Mandauaca vocabulary gives only location and consonant remarks ('Se parece mucho al Baniba, salvo que en algunas voces usan la J gutural en lugar de la B ó de la P de aquel. La Sh como en inglés y la R siempre suave'); the only accent remark in the book's Arawak notes ('El acento es llano', p. 53 n. 1) is about Baniba, not Mandauaca. Some Mandauaca words carry acute accents; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Aikhenvald, Alexandra Y. 1995. Bare. Languages of the World/Materials 100. Munich: LINCOM Europa.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (downloaded when we checked the sources)
sources.note: Her informant stated Baré and Mandawaka were mutually intelligible (Fabre; en.wikipedia); the Bare sketch may carry notes on Mandawaka and its relation to Baré stress (Baré has contrastive stress per Aikhenvald 1999).

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2020. Enciclopédia das línguas Arawak: acrescida de seis novas línguas e dois bancos de dados, vol. II, ch. 14 (Warekena, Mandawaka), pp. 87-206. Curitiba: Editora CRV.

sources.note: Only post-2001 treatment; Glottolog's subclassification source for mand1448; Ramirez's 2020 volumes give phoneme inventories including an accent phoneme for other poorly attested languages (e.g. Kauixana per pt.wikipedia), so a Mandawaka phonology sketch with an accent remark is plausible here.

sources.citation: González Ñáñez, Omar. 2000. Las lenguas indígenas del Amazonas venezolano. In F. Queixalós & O. Renault-Lescure (eds.), As línguas amazônicas hoje, 385-418. São Paulo: ISA/IRD/MPEG.

sources.note: Survey that treats Mandawaka as the Casiquiare variant of Baré (extinct in Venezuela); would settle the identity question rather than stress.
